#### Native C++ route

The recipe above prototypes a reconstruction in Python and selects a built-in one by name; it stays the one
recipe. A new scheme that the solver itself runs is built into the library and selected from the YAML card, and
this route is the one place that says how, for a reconstruction and for a Riemann solver. There is one
reconstruction module and one Riemann module: a new scheme is a new entry in their tables and a new face function,
not a new class. Each step below is a fact of the code at the pin.

**Select it from YAML.** A reconstruction is read from `dynamics/reconstruct/vertical` for $x_1$ and from
`dynamics/reconstruct/horizontal` for $x_2$ and $x_3$, into `recon1` and `recon23` ([`src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp:28-31`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp#L28-L31)). Each section takes `shock`, `type` and
`scale`, and a missing key keeps its default ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:208-211`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L208-L211)); `type` defaults to `dc` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.hpp:41`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.hpp#L41)):

```cpp
  check_keys(node, path, keys);
  op->shock() = node["shock"].as<bool>(op->shock());
  op->interp()->type() = node["type"].as<std::string>(op->interp()->type());
  op->interp()->scale() = node["scale"].as<bool>(op->interp()->scale());
  ADD_ARG(std::string, type) = "dc";
```

A Riemann solver is read from `dynamics/riemann-solver`, whose keys are `type` and `dir` ([`src/riemann/riemann.cpp:67`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.cpp#L67)). A
missing key keeps the created `type` and `dir` ([`src/riemann/riemann.cpp:71-72`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.cpp#L71-L72)), and so does a card with no `riemann-solver`
section ([`src/riemann/riemann.cpp:59`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.cpp#L59)); the created `type` is `hllc` ([`src/riemann/riemann.hpp:61`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.hpp#L61)):

```cpp

  op->dir() = node["dir"].as<std::string>(op->dir());
  if (!config[section]["riemann-solver"]) return op;
```

**Lookup.** A reconstruction name maps to one value of the `Scheme` enum ([`src/recon/recon_point.h:19`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/recon_point.h#L19)), compared as a
string, branch by branch, in `parse_scheme` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:17-26`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L17-L26)); a name with no branch is refused by a `TORCH_CHECK`
when the block is built ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:25`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L25)):

```cpp
enum class Scheme : int { dc, plm, ppm, cp3, weno3, cp5, weno5 };
Scheme parse_scheme(std::string const& type) {
  if (type == "dc") return Scheme::dc;
  if (type == "plm") return Scheme::plm;
  if (type == "ppm") return Scheme::ppm;
  if (type == "cp3") return Scheme::cp3;
  if (type == "weno3") return Scheme::weno3;
  if (type == "cp5") return Scheme::cp5;
  if (type == "weno5") return Scheme::weno5;
  TORCH_CHECK(false, "Interp: unknown type " + type);
}
```

The module is created twice, under the names `interp1` (density and species) and `interp2` (velocity and
pressure) ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:242-244`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L242-L244)); `interp2` takes its partner scheme from `velocity_pressure_scheme` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:28-32`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L28-L32)):

```cpp
  pinterp1 = InterpImpl::create(options->interp(), s, this, "interp1");
  pinterp2 = InterpImpl::create(options->interp(), velocity_pressure_scheme(s),
                                this, "interp2");
Scheme velocity_pressure_scheme(Scheme s) {
  return s == Scheme::weno3   ? Scheme::cp3
         : s == Scheme::weno5 ? Scheme::cp5
                              : s;
}
```

A Riemann name maps to one value of the `RiemannKind` enum ([`src/riemann/riemann.hpp:20-27`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.hpp#L20-L27)) in `parse_riemann_kind`
([`src/riemann/riemann.cpp:77-85`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.cpp#L77-L85)); a name with no branch is refused by a `TORCH_CHECK` when the block is built
([`src/riemann/riemann.cpp:84`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.cpp#L84)):

```cpp
enum class RiemannKind : int {
  hllc,
  lmars,
  roe,
  shallow_roe,
  upwind,
  plume_roe
};
RiemannKind parse_riemann_kind(std::string const& type) {
  if (type == "hllc") return RiemannKind::hllc;
  if (type == "lmars") return RiemannKind::lmars;
  if (type == "roe") return RiemannKind::roe;
  if (type == "shallow-roe") return RiemannKind::shallow_roe;
  if (type == "upwind") return RiemannKind::upwind;
  if (type == "plume-roe") return RiemannKind::plume_roe;
  TORCH_CHECK(false, "RiemannSolver: unknown type " + type);
}
```

**Add a reconstruction.** Besides the enum value and its `parse_scheme` branch, a stencil scheme needs its width
and coefficient counts in `SchemeTraits` ([`src/recon/recon_point.h:25-39`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/recon_point.h#L25-L39)):

```cpp
template <Scheme S>
struct SchemeTraits {
  static constexpr int stencil =
      S == Scheme::dc                                              ? 1
      : S == Scheme::plm || S == Scheme::cp3 || S == Scheme::weno3 ? 3
                                                                   : 5;
  static constexpr int ncoeff = S == Scheme::cp3     ? 3
                                : S == Scheme::weno3 ? 12
                                : S == Scheme::cp5   ? 5
                                : S == Scheme::weno5 ? 48
                                                     : 0;
  static constexpr int ncoeff_nu = S == Scheme::cp5     ? 5
                                   : S == Scheme::weno5 ? 48
                                                        : 0;
};
```

its coefficient table, built in `InterpImpl::reset` as for `cp3` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:51-55`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L51-L55)):


([`src/recon/recon_point.h:152-165`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/recon_point.h#L152-L165)):

```cpp
template <Scheme S, typename T, bool Nu = false>
DISPATCH_MACRO inline T recon_point(T const* src, int stride, T const* row,
                                    bool scale) {
  if constexpr (S == Scheme::cp3) {
    return poly_point<T, 3>(src, stride, row);
  } else if constexpr (S == Scheme::cp5) {
    return poly_point<T, 5>(src, stride, row);
  } else if constexpr (S == Scheme::weno3) {
    return weno3_point(src, stride, row, scale);
  } else {
    static_assert(S == Scheme::weno5, "dc, plm and ppm are tensor code");
    return weno5_point<T>(src, stride, row, scale);
  }
}
```

**Face slots: which state is left and which is right.** The two slots of the reconstruction result are named
`ILT` and `IRT` by this enum ([`src/snap.h:44-45`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/snap.h#L44-L45)):

```cpp
  ILT = 0,  //!< Left interface
  IRT = 1,  //!< Right interface
```

Face $i$ is the face on the low side of cell $i$, between cells $i-1$ and $i$. The reconstruction hands the
interpolant two slices of the result, `outl` and `outr` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:221-224`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L221-L224)):

```cpp
  auto outl = wlr[IRT].slice(dim, il - 1, iu + 1);
  auto outr = wlr[ILT].slice(dim, il, iu + 2);

  pinterp->forward(w, dim, outl, outr);
```

so `left`, the value at each cell's low-side face, lands in slot `IRT` at the cell's own index, and `right`, the
value at each cell's high-side face, lands in slot `ILT` one index on. At index $i$, slot `ILT` holds the state
on the left of face $i$, from cell $i-1$, and slot `IRT` the state on its right, from cell $i$; step 5 of the
recipe shows exactly this. The sweep passes slot `ILT` as `wl` and slot `IRT` as `wr` to `priemann` ([`src/hydro/sweep.cpp:115-116`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/hydro/sweep.cpp#L115-L116)), and the
flux at index $i$ is the flux through face $i$: the update of cell $i$ uses the fluxes at $i$ and $i+1$, each
times its face area `area1` ([`src/coord/coordinate.cpp:614-615`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L614-L615)):

```cpp
    hydro.priemann->forward(lr[ILT], lr[IRT], dim, flux, face_pressure,
                            central);
  return area1.slice(-1, si + 1, ei + 1) * flux1.slice(-1, si + 1, ei + 1) -
         area1.slice(-1, si, ei) * flux1.slice(-1, si, ei);
```

**Riemann shapes and face pressure.** The $x_1$ flux `_flux1` is the flux register's total for direction 1
([`src/hydro/hydro.cpp:240`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L240)). The $x_1$ face pressure `_face_pressure1` is a float64 buffer of the full block, ghosts
included, one row only, and absent when the block has one cell along $x_1$ ([`src/hydro/hydro.cpp:252-254`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L252-L254)):

```cpp
  _flux1 = register_buffer("F1", freg.totals()[0]);
  _face_pressure1 = register_buffer(
      "P1", nc1 > 1 ? torch::zeros({nc3, nc2, nc1}, torch::kFloat64)
                    : torch::Tensor());
```

The left and right states have the shape of the state, as the reconstruction result above has. The solver writes
the face pressure into `face_pressure_out`: the tensor it is given, or a scratch tensor of one row when it is
given none ([`src/riemann/riemann.cpp:305`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/riemann/riemann.cpp#L305)):

```cpp
    face_pressure_out = direct ? face_pressure : torch::empty_like(wl[IDN]);
```

geometry ignores `face_pressure1` ([`src/coord/coordinate.cpp:698`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/coord/coordinate.cpp#L698)).

**Shapes, outputs and device.**

- Reconstruction output: the result is allocated like the input, so it has the input's dtype and device, and the
  interpolant writes into `result` ([`src/recon/reconstruct.cpp:255`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/src/recon/reconstruct.cpp#L255)):

- In place: the solver writes the flux into the tensor it is given without resizing it; every operand shares one

**Rebuild.** Build the library with `cmake` ([`README.md:102-103`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/README.md#L102-L103)) and reinstall the Python package with `pip`
([`README.md:106-108`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062/README.md#L106-L108)):

```bash
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DNETCDF=ON
cmake --build build --parallel 3
pip install .
```

Then set the new name as `type` under `dynamics/reconstruct/vertical` or `horizontal`, or under
`dynamics/riemann-solver`.

**Check the registration.** This test builds a block from the repository deck with the names selected, and fails
when a name has no branch in `parse_scheme` or `parse_riemann_kind`. Run it from the repository root with the
rebuilt package, with the new names in place of `weno5` and `lmars`:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import snapy
import yaml

def selects(recon, riemann):
    """Build a block selecting these names; raises if one is unknown."""
    deck = yaml.safe_load(Path("examples/straka_single.yaml").read_text())
    deck["dynamics"]["reconstruct"] = {
        "vertical": {"type": recon},
        "horizontal": {"type": recon},
    }
    deck["dynamics"]["riemann-solver"] = {"type": riemann}
    Path("check.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(deck))
    options = snapy.MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml("check.yaml")
    return snapy.MeshBlock(options)

selects("weno5", "lmars")
try:
    selects("weno5", "mine")
except RuntimeError as err:
    assert "RiemannSolver: unknown type mine" in str(err)
else:
    raise AssertionError("an unregistered name was accepted")
print("N6 scheme: the selected names are registered")
```
